heroHeadline: GSMA/Huawei Report Finds 3.1 Billion Covered People Still Offline as Nigeria, India and South Africa Advance Literacy and Infrastructure Programs
heroSubtitle: GSMA Intelligence and Huawei's September 10, 2026 report 'Bridging the Divide' found that despite 96% global mobile broadband coverage, 3.1 billion covered people (38%) remain offline — identifying digital literacy, not infrastructure, as the dominant barrier and estimating $3.5 trillion in potential GDP gains by 2030. The same day, India's Digital Bharat Nidhi signed an Amended BharatNet Phase III agreement to extend fibre broadband across 26,777 villages in Jharkhand. Nigeria's Federal Government selected the first 16,000-learner cohort for its Digital Training Academy on September 9 from 72,850 applicants, and Vodacom marked International Literacy Day (September 8) by disclosing its TechStart programme has trained over 400,000 young people across Africa since 2024. In the US, NTIA issued a BEAD Supplemental Deployment Policy Notice on September 3 letting states redirect broadband savings toward previously unserved locations.
footerNote: Data sourced from ITU, GSMA, World Bank/IFC, A4AI, SpaceX, NTIA/FCC, Government of India, and major international research outlets. Contested figures noted with confidence levels.
